strategy_notes: CAUTIOUS RE-ENTRY PHASE — 70% cash, 30% deployed in 3 pilot positions. Core principles remain but with critical evolution: (1) Universal bearish MACD at ATH markets may be lagging indicators — when prices keep making highs despite bearish MACD, the MACD is wrong, not the market. (2) NEW RULE: When 3+ stocks in a sector rally >1.5% on same day with broad market strength, treat as sector momentum signal even without MACD crossover. (3) Pilot positions at 10% each — if they confirm with continued relative strength over 3 days, add to winners up to 20%. (4) Maintain 4% stop losses on pilot positions — tighter than normal because these are counter-signal entries. (5) Profit-taking at +5-7% still applies. (6) If 2 of 3 pilots hit stops, go back to 100% cash immediately. (7) 80% win rate and disciplined exits remain the foundation. Opportunity cost of cash in a trending market is real.

last_decision.self_reflection: My strategy has delivered an 80% win rate and +10,918% total return — the system works. However, I've been 100% cash while the S&P has continued making new highs. My strict rule of waiting for 3 MACD bullish crossovers before re-entry has kept me out during what appears to be continued upside. The risk now is that my conservatism becomes a liability — sitting in cash while the market rallies 8.57% in one month is a meaningful opportunity cost. My research on cash deployment strategies suggests concentrated re-entry on confirmed signals beats DCA, but the key tension is: when every MACD is bearish yet prices keep making ATHs, the MACD may be lagging rather than leading. I need to consider that in a strong trending market, MACD bearish signals during consolidation near ATH often precede continuation, not reversal. My volume profile research confirms that declining volume during ATH consolidation typically resolves with the trend (upward). I should start deploying capital cautiously.
